[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This playbook is the single sequencing entry point for Platform Engineering teams authoring a new Golden Path bundle from inception to ARB approval. It defines which of the six bundle components to author, in which order, what must be true before each component is started, what outputs each component produces that downstream components depend on, and when concurrent authoring is safe versus when it creates rework.

This document describes what **Platform Engineering does when creating a new path**. It is the authoring counterpart to [GUID-GOV-PROC-003](GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md), which describes what product engineering teams do when *consuming* a published path. The catalog lifecycle governance model — proposal approval, versioning policy, ARB process, and deprecation — is defined in [PTN-GOV-AI-001](../../../../patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-001-golden-path-catalog-governance-pattern.md).
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- Eliminates the most common source of authoring rework: starting a downstream component before its upstream prerequisites are finalized, then having to retroactively update manifests, check IDs, or output references when the upstream component changes
- Provides a single checklist-driven sequencing view that Platform Engineering can track against during a sprint — each phase has unambiguous entry criteria, exit criteria, and a deliverable
- Surfaces the concurrent-authoring window (Phases 4–5) explicitly so teams can parallelize safely without coordination failures

#### Applicable Scenarios

- Authoring a brand-new Golden Path bundle for submission to the ARB for the first time
- Releasing a major breaking version (`vX.0.0`) of an existing path that changes one or more bundle components — the authoring sequence applies to the changed components and to any downstream components that depend on their outputs
- Adding a new language variant to an existing path (e.g., adding a Python scaffold to a path that previously only had a .NET scaffold) — applies at Phase 4b only; Phases 1–3 are not required if the Verification Contract and infrastructure module are unchanged

#### Scope Boundaries

- **In Scope**: The six bundle components, their authoring sequence, inter-component output dependencies, concurrent-authoring constraints, per-component pre-submission checklists, and the ARB submission assembly process

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#business-drivers]

#### Business Drivers

- **Catalog trustworthiness requires structural completeness**: A Verification Contract without a pipeline template that enforces it is advisory. A scaffold without a security template is non-compliant. The six bundle components form an interlocked system — a path is not ready for ARB submission until all six components are complete and have been validated together
- **Regulated environment demands auditability by construction**: HIPAA, FedRAMP, and ARC-AMPE paths must produce compliance evidence on every build. Compliance evidence depends on the pipeline template (Stage 17), the compliance metadata file, and the Compliance Evidence Store all being designed in coordination — components authored in isolation produce incompatible evidence schemas that require manual reconciliation at audit time
- **Autonomous AI agents require a constrained solution space**: As documented in the [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md), AI coding agents operate within the Golden Path's constraints. A path with a missing or incomplete bundle component is not a constraint boundary — it is a partial constraint that agents will navigate around or violate by defaulting to unconstrained choices

#### Bundle Component Map

A Golden Path bundle consists of exactly six components. Every component has a normative pattern that defines its specification and an authoring guidance document that operationalizes it:

| Component | Normative Pattern | Authoring Guidance | Key Manifest |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Verification Contract** | PTN-GOV-AI-003 | GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 | `{path-id}-verification-contract.yaml` |
| **Infrastructure Module** | PTN-INFRA-GOV-003 | GUID-INFRA-IMPL-001 | `infrastructure-module-manifest.yaml` |
| **Application Scaffold** | PTN-APP-GOV-004 | GUID-APP-IMPL-003 | `scaffold.yaml` |
| **CI/CD Pipeline Template** | PTN-TECH-GOV-001 | GUID-TECH-IMPL-001 | `workflow-params.yaml` |
| **Security Template** | PTN-SEC-GOV-001 | GUID-SEC-IMPL-001 | `security-template-manifest.yaml` |
| **Compliance Metadata** | PTN-GOV-AI-006 | GUID-GOV-IMPL-002 | `compliance-metadata.yaml` |

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#inter-component-output-dependencies]

#### Inter-Component Output Dependencies

The critical authoring constraint is that several components consume outputs produced by upstream components. Authoring a downstream component before its upstream outputs are finalized forces rework when the upstream changes:

```
Verification Contract
    │
    ├─ Layer 1 check IDs ──────────────────────► Pipeline Template (Stage 2)
    ├─ Layer 2 check IDs ──────────────────────► Pipeline Template (Stage 9)
    └─ Layer 3 check IDs ──────────────────────► Pipeline Template (Stage 10) + Security Template (OPA-001–007)
                │
Infrastructure Module
    │
    ├─ namespace_name ─────────────────────────► Scaffold (scaffold.yaml path constants)
    ├─ workload_identity_ref ──────────────────► Security Template (service-account manifest)
    ├─ secrets_store_uri ──────────────────────► Scaffold (scaffold.yaml path constants)
    └─ isolation_enforcement_level ────────────► Compliance Metadata (Layer 2a evidence ref)
                │
Scaffold + Pipeline Template + Security Template  ◄─── Concurrent authoring window
    │
    ├─ Scaffold unit test invocation pattern ──► Pipeline Template (Stage 3 configuration)
    ├─ Pipeline evidence artifact paths ───────► Compliance Metadata (artifact path references)
    └─ Security manifest control mappings ─────► Compliance Metadata (regulatory control rows)
                │
Compliance Metadata  ◄─── Always last; depends on artifact-level details from all other five
```

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#current-state-assessment]

#### Current State Assessment

Most Platform Engineering teams attempting to author a new path without a sequencing guide begin Verification Contract, Scaffold, and Pipeline Template simultaneously. The scaffold uses placeholder namespace and secrets store values that require update after the infrastructure module is applied; the pipeline references check IDs that change as the Verification Contract is finalized; the compliance metadata is authored after the fact and references evidence artifact paths that the pipeline writes to different locations. Each retroactive fix requires re-running pre-submission validation.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#future-state-vision]

#### Future State Vision

With this playbook, all Platform Engineering teams author bundle components in a documented sequence with explicit entry and exit criteria for each phase. Pre-submission validation for each component passes on the first submission to EA Practice review. ARB submission packages are structurally complete — no missing components, no stale cross-component references, no compliance metadata in placeholder state.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#problem-description]

#### Problem Description

The six authoring guidance documents (GUID-GOV-IMPL-001, GUID-INFRA-IMPL-001, GUID-APP-IMPL-003, GUID-TECH-IMPL-001, GUID-SEC-IMPL-001, GUID-GOV-IMPL-002) each define the authoring process for one component. They reference each other's prerequisite relationships in their Related Guidance sections. But no single document tells a Platform Engineering author: (1) which component to start first, (2) which components can safely be authored concurrently, (3) what specific output values must be harvested from one component before the next can begin, or (4) when the bundle is ready to assemble into an ARB submission package.

GUID-GOV-PROC-003 explicitly states it does not cover path authoring, directing readers to PTN-GOV-AI-001. PTN-GOV-AI-001 covers the catalog governance lifecycle (proposal → ARB → publication versioning), not the component authoring sequence. The gap is the sequencing document that bridges the governance lifecycle and the per-component guidance.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#impact-assessment]

#### Impact Assessment

- An author who begins the scaffold before the infrastructure module is applied must replace placeholder `namespace_name` and `secrets_store_uri` values in `scaffold.yaml` after the fact — typically discovered during the scaffold's pre-submission dry-run validation, which requires a Phase 4b restart
- An author who begins the pipeline template before the Verification Contract Layer 1 and Layer 2 check IDs are finalized must update the `conformance-check` and `fitness-function-runner` command invocations each time the contract changes
- An author who authors the compliance metadata file before the pipeline template's Stage 17 evidence artifact paths are confirmed will have mismatched `artifact_path` references in `compliance-metadata.yaml`, causing the Compliance Evidence Store to report missing evidence for every build

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#principle-1-verification-contract-first]

#### Principle 1: Verification Contract First

**Description:** The Verification Contract must be authored through at least Phase 3 of GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 (all Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3 check IDs finalized with agreed check commands) before any other bundle component authoring begins.

**Rationale:** Every other component is downstream of the Verification Contract. The Pipeline Template executes Layer 1 check IDs at Stage 2 and Layer 2 check IDs at Stage 9. The Security Template's OPA policy bundle is parameterized against Layer 3 check IDs. The Infrastructure Module's TF checks are validated against Layer 3 policy. If the contract changes after downstream components are started, each downstream component must be updated and re-validated. The cost of a contract change after pipeline authoring has begun is significantly higher than the cost of fully finalizing the contract before beginning.

**Application:** Gate the start of all other component authoring on receipt of the Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3 check ID inventory from GUID-GOV-IMPL-001. Do not treat a draft or partial contract as a start signal for downstream components. The exact check commands (`conformance-check --checks CC-001,CC-002,...`, `fitness-function-runner --checks FF-001,...`) must be confirmed.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#principle-2-infrastructure-module-outputs-gate-three-downstream-components]

#### Principle 2: Infrastructure Module Outputs Gate Three Downstream Components

**Description:** The Infrastructure Module must be applied in a staging environment and its four required outputs harvested before the Scaffold, Security Template, or Pipeline Template can be fully parameterized. The outputs are `namespace_name`, `workload_identity_ref`, `secrets_store_uri`, and `isolation_enforcement_level`.

**Rationale:** These are not configurable values teams provide — they are path constants baked into the scaffold's `scaffold.yaml`, the security template's service account manifest, and the pipeline's deployment configuration. A placeholder value in any of these manifests will cause a runtime failure when the path is first adopted by a service team.

**Application:** Follow GUID-INFRA-IMPL-001 through Phase 6 (staging apply and output capture) before beginning Phases 4a (Scaffold) or 4b (Security Template). Record the four output values in the path's internal tracking document; they are required inputs to Phases 4a, 4b, and 4c.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#principle-3-the-concurrent-window-is-explicit-and-bounded]

#### Principle 3: The Concurrent Window Is Explicit and Bounded

**Description:** Phases 4a (Scaffold), 4b (Pipeline Template), 4c (Security Template), and 4d (Compliance Metadata) may be authored concurrently, but each has specific inputs it needs from upstream components that must be confirmed before it begins. Compliance Metadata (4d) must always complete after the other three have finished, because it depends on the artifact paths the Pipeline Template writes and the control mappings the Security Template defines.

**Rationale:** Concurrent authoring compresses calendar time. The constraints exist because the components share input values — if two authors work concurrently and one discovers a change to a shared value, the other must be notified and their in-progress work updated. Managing three concurrent workstreams is feasible; starting them without confirmed inputs produces coordination failures that cost more time than the parallelism saves.

**Application:** Confirm all inputs for each concurrent component before assigning it to an author. Scaffold author needs: `namespace_name`, `secrets_store_uri`, and the check IDs for any scaffold-specific Layer 1 checks. Pipeline Template author needs: all Layer 1 and Layer 2 check IDs, the scaffold's unit test invocation pattern, and confirmed OIDC workload identity environment variable names. Security Template author needs: `workload_identity_ref`, `namespace_name`, and all Layer 3 check IDs.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#principle-4-compliance-metadata-is-always-the-final-authoring-step]

#### Principle 4: Compliance Metadata Is Always the Final Authoring Step

**Description:** The Compliance Metadata file (`compliance-metadata.yaml`) maps regulatory controls to the specific artifacts — manifest paths, OPA check IDs, evidence artifact paths — that evidence those controls. It cannot be authored accurately until all five other components are complete, because it references the artifact paths those components produce.

**Rationale:** A compliance metadata file authored before the Pipeline Template's Stage 17 evidence artifact paths are confirmed will reference incorrect paths. The Compliance Evidence Store queries evidence by `path_id`, `artifact_path`, and `control_id`. Mismatched paths produce missing-evidence gaps in automated compliance reports and require manual remediation at audit time.

**Application:** Begin GUID-GOV-IMPL-002 Phase 1 (control inventory) concurrently with Phases 4a–4c, but do not complete Phase 2 (artifact mapping) until all artifact paths, manifest file paths, and OPA check IDs are confirmed from the other five components. Use Phase 1's manifest-to-control mapping table as a shared input for the Security Template author — the control rows the Security Template must substantiate are defined here.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#principle-5-a-golden-path-scopes-to-one-workload--not-an-end-to-end-solution]

#### Principle 5: A Golden Path Scopes to One Workload — Not an End-to-End Solution

**Description:** A Golden Path is a blueprint for a single deployable workload unit of a specific architectural type. It is not a blueprint for a complete business solution. A business solution will typically be composed of multiple workloads, each independently built from an appropriate Golden Path.

**Rationale:** Conflating solution scope with workload scope produces paths that are too broad to be parameterizable, too opinionated to be reusable, and too coupled to be governed cleanly. The catalog's value comes from each path being a discrete, well-bounded unit — a team selects the right path for each workload they build, not a single path for the whole system.

**Application:** When authoring the path proposal (Phase 1), the workload class must name a single deployable unit archetype (e.g., `hipaa-rest-microservice`, `event-driven-consumer`, `scheduled-batch-job`) — not a solution domain (e.g., "member eligibility system"). If a business solution requires five workloads, the correct answer is five Golden Path instantiations — potentially from the same path, potentially from different paths — not one path that ties them together.

**Boundary test:** Ask: "Can this workload be deployed, versioned, and retired independently of other workloads?" If yes, it is a valid Golden Path workload. If no, the path is scoping a dependency graph rather than a workload, and the proposal should be decomposed.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#principle-6-persistent-data-stores-are-not-part-of-the-workload-path-bundle]

#### Principle 6: Persistent Data Stores Are Not Part of the Workload Path Bundle

**Description:** Golden Path infrastructure modules provision the workload's runtime environment (isolation boundary, identity, secrets access). They do not provision the workload's persistent data store (relational database, document store, cache, message broker, search index, etc.). Data store provisioning is a separate concern — owned either by the Platform Engineering team as a shared platform resource, or by a future dedicated data-store Golden Path.

**Rationale:** Bundling a data store into a workload Golden Path couples the workload's deployment lifecycle to its data tier, creates infrastructure modules that are too large to be verified atomically, and violates the principle that each workload owns and manages its data independently. The secrets store integration already wired into every path is how the workload *accesses credentials* for its data store — the data store itself is provisioned and governed separately.

**Application:**
- The infrastructure module provisions: workload isolation boundary, workload identity, and least-privilege secrets store access.
- The infrastructure module does **not** provision: relational databases, document stores, caches, search indexes, message brokers, or any other persistent or stateful data store.
- If the path's target workload requires a persistent data store, document in the proposal that data store provisioning is out of scope for this path. Teams provisioning a new workload from the path request their data store through the approved platform provisioning process.
- A data-store Golden Path (scoped to a specific data store workload class) is a legitimate future catalog entry but is a separate path authored and governed independently — it is not a component of the application workload path.

**Verification Contract implication:** Do not include data store connectivity checks (e.g., "database connection is healthy") in the path's Verification Contract. Data store connectivity is a workload-specific runtime concern the team addresses in their own workload's observable behavior — it is not a path-level structural rule that every workload of this class must satisfy.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#principle-7-end-to-end-dry-run-validates-the-complete-bundle]

#### Principle 7: End-to-End Dry Run Validates the Complete Bundle

**Description:** Before assembling the ARB submission package, the complete bundle must pass an end-to-end dry run: a scaffold-instantiated test service runs the full pipeline against a staging environment, all 17 pipeline stages pass, all conformance checks pass, and a compliance evidence record is confirmed in the Compliance Evidence Store.

**Rationale:** Components developed and validated individually may have integration failures when assembled: the scaffold's test invocation pattern may not match what the Pipeline Template's Stage 3 expects; the Security Template's OPA check IDs in `security-template-manifest.yaml` may not match what the Verification Contract Layer 3 section declares; the Compliance Metadata's artifact paths may not match what the pipeline writes at Stage 17. Integration validation is the only way to confirm that an assembled bundle functions as a system.

**Application:** Use `dry_run: true` for the first end-to-end run to validate all verification stages without affecting any environment. Set `dry_run: false` for the final validation run; the ARB submission package must include the run ID of a `dry_run: false` successful pipeline execution and the confirmed Compliance Evidence Store entry.

#### Approach 1: Sequential-then-Concurrent (Recommended)

**Overview:** Author the Verification Contract (Phase 2) and Infrastructure Module (Phase 3) sequentially — each must reach its exit criteria before the next begins. Once both are complete and infrastructure outputs are harvested, begin the three middle components (Scaffold, Pipeline Template, Security Template) concurrently. Author Compliance Metadata last.

**When to Use:** All new Golden Path bundles. All major version updates where the Verification Contract or Infrastructure Module changes.

**Structure:**
```
Phase 1: Proposal Approval (1–3 days)
Phase 2: Verification Contract [sequential, blocks all] (5–7 days)
Phase 3: Infrastructure Module [sequential, blocks Scaffold + Security Template] (7–10 days)
Phase 4a–4c: Scaffold + Pipeline Template + Security Template [concurrent] (7–10 days)
Phase 4d: Compliance Metadata [sequential, after 4a–4c complete] (3–5 days)
Phase 5: End-to-End Validation (2–3 days)
Phase 6: ARB Package Assembly and Submission (1–2 days)
```
**Target total**: 25–35 working days for a greenfield HIPAA path.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#approach-2-incremental-variant-addition]

#### Approach 2: Incremental (Variant Addition)

**Overview:** For adding a language variant scaffold to an existing published path, skip Phases 1–3, begin at Phase 4a, and update only the affected components (Scaffold and Pipeline Template). Compliance Metadata is updated to add the new language variant's artifact paths.

**When to Use:** Adding a Python or Java variant to a path that already has a .NET scaffold. The Verification Contract and Infrastructure Module are assumed unchanged.

**Considerations:** If the new variant requires a new Layer 1 check (e.g., a Python-specific import policy check), the Verification Contract must be updated first, which triggers a minor path version bump and requires GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 Phase 3 to be re-run before the pipeline template can be updated.
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#approach-3-minor-version-update-non-breaking-change]

#### Approach 3: Minor Version Update (Non-Breaking Change)

**Overview:** For non-breaking changes to a published path — adding an optional check, bumping a tool version, adding a new optional stage — only the affected components need to be re-authored and validated. The full 6-phase greenfield sequence does not apply.

**When to Use:** Any path update that does not change required field names, remove existing checks, change output names, or alter the compliance scope. Determined by PTN-GOV-AI-001 §Governance Decision Guide.

**Phases that apply:**
```
Phase 1 (abbreviated): Open a PR with the change scope description; no ARB proposal required
Phase 2: Only if check IDs change or new checks are added to the Verification Contract
Phase 3: Only if the Infrastructure Module IaC changes
Phase 4a-4d: Only the component(s) that change; per-component pre-submission checklist still required
Phase 5: End-to-end dry_run: false still required — never skip Phase 5 for a published path
Phase 6 (abbreviated): Platform Engineering Lead approval only; ARB notification (not review)
```
**Key constraint:** Phase 5 is always required regardless of how small the change. A tool version bump in Stage 7 that changes scan output format will break Stage 17 evidence artifact paths — an integration failure that only Phase 5 catches.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#approach-4-major-version-update-breaking-change]

#### Approach 4: Major Version Update (Breaking Change)

**Overview:** Breaking changes require the full ARB review cycle, a migration guide authored before publication, and a 90-day migration window for existing adopters per PTN-GOV-AI-001.

**When to Use:** Any change that renames outputs, removes required fields, changes compliance scope, alters the Verification Contract check ID set, or changes the artifact management endpoint.

**Phases that apply:** All six phases, same as greenfield. The additional requirement is a migration guide (see PTN-GOV-AI-001 Example 4 for the required template structure) published at `catalog/changelogs/{path-id}/migration-{old}-to-{new}.md` before Phase 6 submission.

- **Record infrastructure module outputs in the path tracking document the moment `terraform apply` completes.** The four values (`namespace_name`, `workload_identity_ref`, `secrets_store_uri`, `isolation_enforcement_level`) are required by three concurrent authors. A delay in distributing these values stalls concurrent work. Capture them immediately.
- **Lock the Verification Contract check ID list before any downstream authoring begins.** The pattern allows check IDs to be assigned final names (e.g., `CC-001`, `FF-002`) in Phase 3 of GUID-GOV-IMPL-001. Author check commands should use the final IDs — not the descriptive names used during Phase 1 design — in all component manifests and pipeline stage configurations.
- **Assign the scaffold and pipeline template to the same author or a tightly coordinated pair.** The scaffold's unit test invocation pattern (test command, test results directory, exit code) must exactly match Stage 3 of the pipeline template. Mismatches discovered during end-to-end validation are the most common single source of Phase 5 failures.
- **Begin the compliance metadata control inventory (GUID-GOV-IMPL-002 Phase 1) at the same time as Phase 4a–4c.** The control inventory does not require finalized artifact paths — it only requires the compliance scope (HIPAA/FedRAMP/none) and the list of regulatory standards. Getting Phase 1 done in parallel with the three middle components means Phase 4d (artifact mapping) can complete quickly once the other three phases exit.
- **Use `dry_run: true` for iteration; use `dry_run: false` exactly once before ARB submission.** The `dry_run: false` run ID is included in the ARB submission package as evidence of a passing end-to-end validation. Running `dry_run: false` multiple times against staging dilutes the evidence value; the single confirmed run is the canonical validation record.

#### Pitfall 1: Starting the Scaffold Before Infrastructure Module Outputs Are Available

**Description:** The scaffold's `scaffold.yaml` requires `namespace_name` and `secrets_store_uri` as path constants. Authors sometimes use placeholder values and plan to update them later.

**Impact:** Every service team that instantiates the scaffold before the path constants are corrected will get a scaffold that fails at the secrets store reference. The update requires a patch version release to the path after initial publication, which forces all early adopters to take a catalog version update PR.

**Prevention:** Gate Phase 4a start on receipt of confirmed infrastructure module outputs. The Phase 3 exit criteria in this playbook must be met before Phase 4a begins.

**Mitigation:** If authoring has already begun with placeholders, grep the scaffold repository for the placeholder values before Phase 5 and replace all instances before the end-to-end dry run.

#### Pitfall 2: Authoring the Pipeline Template Before Scaffold Unit Tests Are Defined

**Description:** Stage 3 of the pipeline template invokes the scaffold's unit test suite. If the scaffold's test framework, test command, and test results directory location are not finalized when the pipeline is authored, Stage 3 is written with a placeholder test command that fails or is inconsistent with what the scaffold actually uses.

**Impact:** The end-to-end dry run (Phase 5) fails at Stage 3. Fixing it requires editing the pipeline template, re-running the PIPE-001 conformance check, and re-generating the `workflow-params.yaml` manifest.

**Prevention:** Confirm the scaffold's unit test invocation pattern with the scaffold author before wiring Stage 3. If authoring concurrently, the scaffold author should define the test framework and test command on Day 1 of Phase 4a and share it explicitly before the pipeline author wires Stage 3.

**Mitigation:** Update Stage 3 and the `workflow-params.yaml` stage description, re-run GUID-TECH-IMPL-001 Phase 3 validation, and re-confirm PIPE-001 before proceeding to Phase 5.

#### Pitfall 3: Finalizing Compliance Metadata Before the Pipeline's Stage 17 Evidence Paths Are Confirmed

**Description:** The Compliance Metadata must reference the exact artifact paths that Stage 17 uploads to the Compliance Evidence Store. If the metadata is authored before Stage 17 is wired (GUID-TECH-IMPL-001 Phase 6), the artifact paths are guessed or placeholder.

**Impact:** The Compliance Evidence Store will report missing evidence for every build until the metadata is corrected — a post-publication breaking change that requires ARB minor review.

**Prevention:** Do not begin GUID-GOV-IMPL-002 Phase 2 (artifact mapping) until Phase 4b (Pipeline Template) has completed Phase 6 validation and the pipeline's Stage 17 evidence upload paths are confirmed.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#phase-1-proposal-approval]

#### Phase 1: Proposal Approval

**Objectives:** Secure ARB authorization to begin authoring a new Golden Path; receive a path ID; confirm compliance scope and workload class.

**Prerequisites:** The business case for the new path is documented; proposed path ID does not conflict with an existing catalog entry.

**Key Activities:**
1. Submit the Golden Path Proposal using the PTN-GOV-AI-001 proposal template, including: workload class, compliance scope, proposed path ID, and the team(s) who will be the first adopters
2. Receive ARB approval and the assigned path ID (format: `GP-NNN`)
3. Create the catalog branch: `catalog/gp-NNN/` with empty placeholder directories for each of the six components

**Workload Scope Decision (required before submission):**

Before submitting the proposal, answer the following questions to confirm the path is scoped to a single workload and not conflating a solution with a path:

| Question | Expected Answer | If Not |
|---|---|---|
| Can the workload be deployed independently without requiring other workloads to be deployed first? | Yes | Decompose — this is a solution, not a workload |
| Does the workload have a single primary runtime artifact (container image, function, job)? | Yes | Decompose — multi-artifact paths are orchestration paths, not workload paths |
| Is a persistent data store part of this path's infrastructure module? | No — data store is provisioned separately | Remove from scope; document the expected provisioning channel in the proposal |
| Does the workload class name identify an architectural archetype (not a business domain)? | Yes — `hipaa-rest-microservice`, not `member-eligibility-system` | Rename to the archetype |

**Data store scope note:** If the proposed workload requires a persistent data store (relational database, document store, cache, etc.), document in the proposal that data store provisioning is **out of scope** for this path. Teams provision their data store through the approved platform provisioning process. If no approved provisioning channel exists for the required data store type, raise this as a dependency in the proposal — it may indicate a future data-store Golden Path is needed, but that would be a separate path authored and governed independently.

**Deliverables:**
- Approved proposal with assigned path ID
- Catalog branch created
- Workload scope decision documented in proposal (single workload confirmed; data store scope noted if applicable)

**Exit Criteria:** Proposal approved; path ID assigned; catalog branch structure created; workload scope boundaries confirmed.

#### Decision Point 1: Can I Start Phase 4a Before Phase 3 is Fully Complete?

**Context:** Phase 3 (Infrastructure Module) takes 7–10 days and Phase 4a–4c are on the critical path. The team is under schedule pressure to compress the timeline.

**Options:**
- Start Phase 4a using placeholder values for `namespace_name` and `secrets_store_uri`; replace them after Phase 3 outputs are confirmed
- Wait for Phase 3 exit criteria to be fully met before starting Phase 4a

**Recommendation:** Wait. Placeholders in `scaffold.yaml` are the most common source of Phase 5 failures. The time saved by starting Phase 4a early is typically less than the time spent on the retroactive find-and-replace and re-validation. The one exception: Phase 4a Phase 1 (scope and language stack confirmation) can be done during Phase 3 — it does not require confirmed output values.

#### Decision Point 2: Are Phases 4b and 4c Safe to Start Before Phase 4a Delivers the Unit Test Invocation Pattern?

**Context:** The pipeline template (4b) needs the scaffold's unit test invocation to wire Stage 3. The scaffold (4a) and pipeline (4b) are concurrent. The 4b author wants to start Stage 3 before the 4a author has confirmed the test command.

**Options:**
- Wire Stage 3 with a placeholder test command and update when 4a author confirms
- Leave Stage 3 empty and wire all other stages first; return to Stage 3 when 4a author confirms

**Recommendation:** Leave Stage 3 empty initially and wire Stages 1–2 and 4–17 first. Stage 3 is stage-sequenced to run after Stage 2 and before Stage 4 — it can be wired last without blocking other stages. Returning to wire one stage is lower risk than wiring it incorrectly and discovering the error at Phase 5.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md#decision-point-3-what-triggers-a-return-to-phase-2]

#### Decision Point 3: What Triggers a Return to Phase 2?

**Context:** During Phase 3. the Infrastructure Module author discovers that the workload isolation approach requires a new structural check (e.g., a finalizer label requirement) that was not anticipated in the Verification Contract.

**Options:**
- Add the check directly to the infrastructure module without updating the Verification Contract
- Return to Phase 2 and add the check to the contract, re-finalize the check IDs, then resume Phase 3

**Recommendation:** Return to Phase 2. A check that exists in the infrastructure module but not in the Verification Contract is an undeclared check — it will fail the Layer 1 conformance gate for any service that instantiates the scaffold because the conformance check runner only knows about checks declared in the contract. Add the check to the contract, get it reviewed and approved, assign it a check ID, then resume Phase 3 with the updated check ID. The delay is typically 1–2 days; the alternative is a broken Layer 1 gate that surfaces at Phase 5 or, worse, at post-publication adoption.

### Real-World Example 1: GP-001 HIPAA REST Microservice Path

**Context:** GP-001 was the first Golden Path authored for the Gainwell catalog. HIPAA compliance scope; .NET REST microservice workload class.

**Challenge:** Phase 2 (Verification Contract) took 10 days because the Layer 3 OPA policy check IDs required co-authorship between infrastructure and security architects — a stakeholder coordination step not anticipated in the initial sprint plan.

**Application:** Phase 3 was held until Layer 3 check IDs were confirmed; this added 3 days beyond the initial timeline but prevented a pipeline-template OPA check command rework cycle.

**Lessons Learned:** For HIPAA paths, budget an additional 2–3 days in Phase 2 for OPA check ID co-authorship between infrastructure and security. The Infrastructure Module author and Security Template author should be included in GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 Phase 3 (check command confirmation) to avoid discovering mismatches later.

### Real-World Example 2: Adding a Python Variant to an Existing Path

**Context:** An existing path (GP-001 .NET) needed a Python language variant scaffold and pipeline template for a data science team.

**Application:** Phases 1–3 were skipped entirely — the Verification Contract and Infrastructure Module were unchanged. Phase 4a (Python scaffold) and Phase 4b (Python pipeline variant) were run concurrently. The Python scaffold used the same `namespace_name` and `secrets_store_uri` values from the existing GP-001 infrastructure module output (already recorded in the path tracking document). Phase 4d (Compliance Metadata) required a minor update to add the Python variant's artifact paths alongside the existing .NET artifact paths.

**Lessons Learned:** The path tracking document's infrastructure output values saved 3 days — the values were already confirmed and did not require a new Phase 3 run. #### Use Case 3: Minor Version Update — Tool Version Bump

**Scenario Description:** Stage 7 (Artifact Security Scan) uses Trivy `0.58.2`. A new version `0.59.0` fixes a false-positive rule and is approved for use. This is a non-breaking minor update.

**Guidance Application (Approach 3):**
1. Open a PR scoped to the pipeline template only; no ARB proposal required
2. Skip Phases 1–3 (Verification Contract and Infrastructure Module are unchanged)
3. Phase 4b only: update the Trivy version pin in Stage 7 and in `workflow-params.yaml`; run GUID-TECH-IMPL-001 pre-submission checklist (PIPE-006 specifically checks tool version pinning)
4. **Phase 5 is required**: run `dry_run: false` end-to-end; confirm the updated Trivy version produces a `reports/artifact-scan.json` that the Stage 17 evidence uploader can parse; confirm Compliance Evidence Store entry is valid
5. Phase 6 (abbreviated): Platform Engineering Lead approves the PR; ARB is notified in the next standing agenda item — no ARB review required

**Key lesson:** Even a single version pin change in Stage 7 requires Phase 5 because tool output format changes between versions can silently break Stage 17 evidence collection.

### Governance Framework

This playbook is the operational process for the catalog authoring lifecycle stage defined in PTN-GOV-AI-001. The EA Practice owns the phase exit criteria; Platform Engineering owns the per-component authoring activities. The ARB approves the completed bundle at Phase 6 — no component of this playbook overrides or replaces the ARB review.

Phase exit criteria are gates enforced by the EA Practice review of the per-component pre-submission checklists. A component is not considered done until the EA Practice reviewer has confirmed the checklist. Self-certification by the authoring team is not sufficient for components that are shared inputs to other components (Verification Contract, Infrastructure Module).
